definitions.explanation: The number 30,000, formed as {三|さん} (three) × {万|まん} (10,000). No sound change occurs — both parts keep their usual readings.

examples.japanese: この{町|まち}の{人口|じんこう}は{約|やく}{三万|さんまん}{人|にん}だ。
examples.english: This town has a population of about thirty thousand.

examples.japanese: {中古|ちゅうこ}の{自転車|じてんしゃ}を{三万|さんまん}{円|えん}で{買|か}ったが、すぐに{修理|しゅうり}が{必要|ひつよう}になった。
examples.english: I bought a used bicycle for thirty thousand yen, but it soon needed repairs.

notes:
Japanese groups large numbers in units of 10,000 ({万|まん}), so 30,000 is "three {万|まん}" rather than "thirty thousand".

COUNTING IN {万|まん}:
- {一万|いちまん}: 10,000 — note {一|いち} is required; {万|まん} alone is not used for 10,000
- {二万|にまん}: 20,000
- {三万|さんまん}: 30,000
- {十万|じゅうまん}: 100,000

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {三万|さんまん}{円|えん}: thirty thousand yen
- {三万|さんまん}{人|にん}: thirty thousand people
- {三万|さんまん}{件|けん}: thirty thousand cases or items
